name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development Induced by Androgens Excess
aliases: 46,XX Disorder of Sex Development with Androgen Overproduction

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XX DSD due to Androgen Excess

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous genitalia at birth including clitoromegaly or labioscrotal fusion
Elevated serum androgens such as 17-hydroxyprogesterone or testosterone in a 46,XX individual
Molecular genetic confirmation of mutations in genes involved in steroidogenesis (e.g., CYP21A2, CYP11B1)
Confirmed 46,XX karyotype without Y chromosome material
Positive family history of congenital adrenal hyperplasia or androgen excess disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia at birth, elevated androgen levels in a 46,XX individual, and genetic confirmation of steroidogenesis gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of ambiguous genitalia and androgen excess.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlarged clitoris present at birth or early infancy
Partial or complete fusion of the labia resembling scrotum

common.notes: Genitalia not clearly male or female
Electrolyte imbalance due to aldosterone deficiency
Excessive terminal hair growth in androgen-sensitive areas

occasional.notes: Menstrual cycle abnormalities in adolescence or adulthood
Rare cystic changes in clitoral tissue

rare.notes: Benign adrenal tumors associated with chronic ACTH stimulation
Rare in some enzyme deficiencies causing excess mineralocorticoids
searchTerms: high blood pressure from mineralocorticoid excess
blood pressure raised by adrenal hormones

rare.notes: Mood disorders related to hormonal imbalances

laboratory: Electrolyte abnormalities (hyponatremia, hyperkalemia) in salt-wasting forms
imaging: Adrenal gland enlargement on ultrasound or CT
Absence of testicular tissue on pelvic ultrasound
other: ACTH stimulation test showing exaggerated steroid precursor response

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent or rudimentary Müllerian structures
Normal or elevated testosterone with androgen receptor defects
Variable genital ambiguity without androgen excess

redFlags: Severe salt-wasting crisis in neonatal period
Rapid virilization in infancy or early childhood
references: Speiser PW, et al. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to steroid 21-hydroxylase deficiency: An Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2018.
Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
